sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by non-permeabilized anti-HA FITC labeling; [³H]RX821002 binding Kd = 3.43 ± 0.58 nM, indistinguishable from untagged receptor; authors explicitly state the tag does not interfere with receptor trafficking, folding, or function.
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly reports an HA tag at the 'extreme amino terminus' of full-length, membrane-anchored α2A-AR and states it does not interfere with trafficking, folding, or function. The topology landmarks confirm residues 1–48 are extracellular with no signal peptide, so insert_after_residue = 0 (prepend before M1) is the only possible N-terminal extracellular junction; residue_after is M (residue 1, read from the numbered sequence). L4 provides quantitative ligand-binding confirmation (Kd preserved), and L2/L3 confirm plasma-membrane surface display by non-permeabilized antibody labeling. The 48-residue extracellular N-terminal span provides ample steric room for a 13–23 aa epitope tag. Full-length α2A-AR with an HA epitope tag at the extreme extracellular amino terminus was expressed in mammalian cells; surface display was confirmed by FITC-conjugated anti-HA antibody labeling under non-permeabilized conditions (L2, L3). Ligand binding was assessed by [³H]RX821002 saturation binding (L4). The topology landmarks place residues 1–48 as extracellular with no signal peptide, so the tag prepends before residue 1 (M). Multiple independent constructs from the same group also place EGFP (RUSH, L6/L7/L8), mCherry (L9), and SNAP-tag (L11) at the same N-terminal position, and a HiBiT construct (IL6-HiBiT-α2A-AR-HaloTag, L10) uses an IL-6 signal peptide to deliver HiBiT to the extracellular N-terminus.

sources.claim: All α 2 -AR constructs possess an extracellular HA epitope tag at the extreme amino terminus where it has previously been shown not to interfere with receptor trafficking, folding or function ( 4 ).

literature_notes: All ledger lines (L1–L11) converge on a single extracellular surface site: the N-terminal prepend. L1–L4 are the primary evidence for α2A-AR specifically, with explicit surface and functional validation. L5–L9 (EGFP, mCherry, RFP, Rluc8 at NT via RUSH) and L11 (SNAP-tag at NT of adrenergic receptors) corroborate the same junction with different tag chemistries. L10 (IL6-HiBiT-α2A-AR-HaloTag) places HiBiT at the extracellular N-terminus via an IL-6 signal peptide; the HaloTag position is not stated in the clip and cannot be pinned, so it is not proposed as a separate site. The C-terminal GFP fusion (L5) is intracellular per the topology landmarks (residues 445–465 = intracellular) and is recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports an insertion in ECL1 (112–121), ECL2 (188–209), or ECL3 (411–424) of this protein, so no internal sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: GFP fused at the C-terminus of full-length α2A-AR (L5); the topology landmarks place residues 445–465 in the intracellular compartment, so this is not a surface tag site.
